data.narrative:
Elroy Air, a Series B autonomous cargo drone operator founded by David Merrill and Clint Cope, commands a current post-money valuation of $800M following $116M in total capital raised. The target operates within the Drones & Autonomous sector, which comprises eight private peers including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Manna Aero, with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given insufficient narrow peer density. A 1.9x step-up multiplier applied to the $800M Series B post-money produces an implied forward valuation of $1.52B. This multiplier reflects typical venture capital mark-up patterns between Series B and subsequent funding rounds. Peer-median comparison was not executable; the broader sector contains four same-stage or adjacent-stage data points insufficient to establish a reliable median, and a cross-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $1.7B, centered on $1.52B. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty: the absence of robust same-stage peer pricing limits confidence in whether the 1.9x multiplier accurately reflects market conditions for autonomous logistics businesses specifically. Critical unknowns include unit economics trajectory, regulatory clearance timelines, and commercial deployment velocity relative to peer benchmarks. Investors should treat this range as directional pending deeper operational and market-share analysis.
